criteria.scenario: Every Go-port commit in the opencodex inventory has been read, not sampled, and 050 records the outcome with the count
criteria.expectedEvidence: explorer return or main-agent reading log naming each SHA, plus the amended 050 section
criteria.capturedEvidence: Explorer read all 44 labeled Go-port rows and ran git patch-id --stable, proving they collapse to 7 unique patches re-landed up to 8 times. The wholesale rejection was WRONG: 3 of the 7 carry uncovered mechanisms and are now cases (icacls-inheritance-r-empty-dacl, tcp-tcb-survives-listener, file-url-encodes-backslash); the other 4 correctly stayed rejected. The A-gate reviewer independently re-ran the patch-id collapse and confirmed the per-patch dispositions. Recorded in 050 and 080; row count corrected from 50 to 44.

criteria.scenario: The 9122d5ebe mechanism is compared against redirected-ps-output-mojibake on the reader's-situation test and the decision is recorded either way
criteria.expectedEvidence: the new case file, or the recorded reasoning in 050 keeping the REF
criteria.capturedEvidence: 9122d5ebe split out as known-folder-empty-not-error rather than remaining a REF on redirected-ps-output-mojibake. Reasoning recorded in 050: mojibake is a value destroyed in transit by a console codepage, this is an API answering an empty string instead of failing. Different fix, different reader. The disposition row was updated in place so opencodex stays at 341/341.

criteria.scenario: Reserved device names and MAX_PATH exist as cases with authoritative Microsoft refs and repros that use nothing but stock Windows
criteria.expectedEvidence: both case files passing lint and validate-graph, each citing a learn.microsoft.com URL
criteria.capturedEvidence: reserved-dos-device-names and max-path-260 written as third-party cases citing learn.microsoft.com, each with a verification note enumerating quoted claims versus inference. The A-gate audit corrected the max-path repro (a 240-char directory under %TEMP% already exceeds the limit) and the lint third-party rule was widened to accept an authoritative vendor doc URL, since citing an unrelated chore commit to satisfy the old rule was worse than citing the spec.
